record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Does any non-abelian variety of ℓ-groups have the amalgamation property?

evidence.quote: 1.27∗ . (W. B. Powell and C. Tsinakis [11] Problem 27(a)) Does any non-abelian variety of ℓ-groups have the amalgamation property?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is an algebraic structure (G, ·, ⁻¹, e, ∧, ∨) such that (G, ·, ⁻¹, e) is a group, (G, ∧, ∨) is a lattice, and the group multiplication distributes over the lattice operations on both sides: x(y ∧ z)w = xyw ∧ xzw and x(y ∨ z)w = xyw ∨ xzw for all x, y, z, w ∈ G. A variety of ℓ-groups is a class of ℓ-groups defined by a set of equations (equivalently, closed under homomorphic images, subalgebras, and direct products). A variety V is said to be non-abelian if it is not contained in the variety of abelian ℓ-groups (i.e., it contains some ℓ-group that is not abelian as a group). A class K of algebras has the amalgamation property if, whenever A, B, C ∈ K and there are embeddings f: A → B and g: A → C, there exist some D ∈ K and embeddings f': B → D and g': C → D such that f' ∘ f = g' ∘ g.

Question: Does there exist a non-abelian variety of ℓ-groups that has the amalgamation property?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Known results show failure of the amalgamation property for the variety of representable ℓ-groups and for certain ℓ-metabelian settings, and only o-approximable ℓ-varieties are candidates. No published resolution establishing or refuting amalgamation for some non-abelian variety of ℓ-groups was located.

status_evidence.title: The failure of the amalgamation property for representable varieties of l-groups
status_evidence.snippet: Failure of amalgamation in the representable variety.
status_evidence.claim: Amalgamation fails for the representable variety of ℓ-groups, leaving the general non-abelian case open.

status_evidence.title: Non-Amalgamation and Conjugation for ℓ-Metabelian Lattice-Ordered Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Negative amalgamation results in the ℓ-metabelian setting.
status_evidence.claim: Further negative results for ℓ-metabelian varieties; the general non-abelian question is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Amalgamations of l-varieties
status_evidence.snippet: Only o-approximable ℓ-varieties can have the amalgamation property; known non-amalgamated formations in o-approximable l-groups are amalgamated in the variety of all lattice-ordered groups.
status_evidence.claim: Reduces candidate non-abelian varieties but does not exhibit a non-abelian variety with the amalgamation property.
